items.title: Is PepsiCo (PEP) Facing A Fresh Challenge In Sports Drinks After Its Poppi Deal?
items.summary: PepsiCo (NasdaqGS:PEP) faces fresh competition as Poppi's founders unveil Jetty, a new hydration drink aimed at Gatorade's turf. Jetty is positioned as a lower sugar and lower sodium option for everyday consumers in the mainstream sports drink category. The launch follows PepsiCo's acquisition of Poppi, creating an unusual rivalry between the buyer and the founders of the acquired brand. items.title: PepsiCo (PEP) Lands Hyatt Deal On A Fair Value Debate
items.summary: Hyatt’s new 10 year food and beverage agreement with PepsiCo (PEP) puts more than 700 U.S. hotels on PepsiCo’s drink and snack roster, giving investors fresh context for the stock’s recent turbulence. PepsiCo’s share price tells a mixed story, with a 30 day share price return of 3.7% but a year to date share price decline of 2.3%. items.title: Coca-Cola’s Valuation Is the Highest in 25 Years. Where Does The Stock Go From Here?
items.summary: Coca-Cola keeps beating earnings estimates, yet investors are paying a price not seen in a quarter century. Between a looming refranchising hit and rivals like PepsiCo and Monster, can the fizz last, or is a stretched multiple about to go flat?

items.title: PepsiCo Has Raised Its Dividend by a Total of 37% Over the Last 5 Years. I Predict $10,000 Invested in It Today Will Pay This Much in Dividends Over the Next Decade.
items.summary: The beverage and snack powerhouse’s stock may be underperforming, but its quarterly payouts keep on coming.

items.title: The Same $10,000 in Pepsi and Coca-Cola Could Produce Very Different Results by 2030
items.summary: One stock just surged 42.5% while its rival barely moved, yet the model sees a surprising gap in where each could land by 2030. Dividends, guidance cuts, and valuation risk all shape which $10,000 stake looks smarter.

items.title: If You Invest $5,000 in Pepsi Today, Here’s What It Could Be Worth by 2030
items.summary: PepsiCo's international snacks are surging while its North American soft drink business stumbles, and Wall St. is split on which story wins. Three scenarios show how far your $5,000 could swing by 2030.

items.title: A $1,500,000 Portfolio in HP, Truist and PepsiCo Pays $65,144 a Year in Dividends. Here’s What Happens if One Cuts
items.summary: Key TakeawaysA hypothetical $1,500,000 portfolio split evenly across HP, Truist Financial and PepsiCo pays about $65,100 a year in dividends at today’s prices, or about $5,430 a month. HP’s dividend looks the safest of the three, taking 28% of free cash flow over the trailing twelve months.
